heroHeadline: House Passes $70B Enforcement Package 215-211; Michigan Supreme Court Bans ICE Courthouse Arrests
heroSubtitle: The U.S. House voted 215-211 on April 30 — with zero Democratic votes — to pass a $70 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package, following the Senate's 50-48 vote on April 23; if enacted it would be the largest single immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history, targeting 100,000+ detention beds and 1 million annual deportations. On the same day, the Michigan Supreme Court approved a rule banning civil arrests — including ICE warrants — at legal proceedings across Michigan, joining Massachusetts, California, and New York. These developments follow the Second Circuit's unanimous April 29 ruling requiring bond hearings for detainees in New York, Connecticut, and Vermont (likely headed to the Supreme Court), the Supreme Court weighing TPS revocations for 350,000 Haitians and 6,000 Syrians, and ICE's FY2026 in-custody death toll reaching a record 29.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, court records, and Congressional records
